claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability during cooling and thermal exposure is governed by kinetic competition between ordered BCC and FCC phase formation.
Diffusion rates of the constituent elements influence the competition between ordered BCC and FCC phase formation.
Changing cooling rate and thermal-exposure conditions changes the diffusion-mediated structural evolution.
Cooling rates from 0.1 to 10 K/s and thermal-exposure temperatures from 500 to 1000°C define the proposed applicability range.
Depending on cooling rate and thermal exposure, ordered BCC, FCC, and potentially intermediate phases will form.
Samples cooled at 10 K/s will be predominantly disordered BCC.
Samples cooled at 0.1 K/s will be predominantly ordered BCC.
Outside cooling rates of 0.1–10 K/s or thermal-exposure temperatures of 500–1000°C, mechanisms other than diffusion-controlled phase competition may dominate.
The relevant elemental diffusion rates and their effects on phase formation are not well understood.
Grain-boundary effects may also affect phase formation.
A lack of dependence of phase fractions and microstructure evolution on cooling rate and thermal exposure would falsify the hypothesis.
